De wereld om ons heen verandert razendsnel. Wat vandaag nieuw is, kan morgen alweer achterhaald zijn. Bij PuurData krijg je de kans om samen met collega’s te werken aan slimme oplossingen voor onze klanten. Zo kun je bijvoorbeeld bedrijven helpen met het inzichtelijk maken van hun data of meedenken over hoe ze veiliger met hun data om kunnen gaan. Je helpt onze klanten vooruit door ze mee te nemen in nieuwe technologieën en te laten zien waar bijvoorbeeld AI daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegt. Op deze manier kun je zowel kleine, maar ook grote en veeleisende bedrijven helpen met oplossingen die kritisch zijn voor hun bedrijfsvoering.  

Tenslotte zorgen wij er samen voor dat jij continu blijft groeien en op de hoogte bent van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen. 

 

Wat ga je doen?  

Als Data Engineer bij PuurData ben je meer dan een technicus. Je bent een consultant die klanten helpt om meer waarde uit hun data te halen. PuurData werkt met platformen zoals Elastic en AWS, en bedient klanten op het gebied van zoektechnologie, observability, security en AI. Jij bent degene die die oplossingen tot leven brengt.

Je start bij de klant. Je inventariseert de vraag: wat willen ze met hun data? Gaat het om betere zoekfunctionaliteit, real-time inzicht in systemen, of security en threat detection? Klanten weten vaak dat er iets niet klopt. Data is traag, er is geen inzicht, of er zijn performance problemen. Maar ze weten niet altijd hoe ze het moeten oplossen. Jij helpt dat helder te maken.

Vervolgens ga je samen met de klant naar de juiste oplossing toe. Je vertaalt de behoefte naar een concrete aanpak en implementeert die van A tot Z: van het inrichten van de datastroom tot het opleveren van dashboards en inzichten.

Geen dag is hetzelfde. De use cases lopen uiteen van zoekoplossingen en business process monitoring tot SIEM-implementaties en data engineering-pipelines. Dat geeft je veel vrijheid in de invulling van je werk.

Continu leren is geen optie, maar de norm
Technologie staat niet stil, en jij ook niet. Bij PuurData is training verplicht. Je blijft op de hoogte van de laatste ontwikkelingen, denk aan Elastic, AI-integraties en nieuwe dataplatformen, en past die kennis direct toe in klantprojecten.


Wie ben jij?

Je bent een ondernemende professional die weinig sturing nodig heeft. Je denkt vanuit de eindgebruiker en streeft naar maximale klanttevredenheid zonder kwaliteit en veiligheid uit het oog te verliezen. Dankzij jouw analytisch vermogen zie je snel de kern van een probleem en kom je met creatieve, structurele oplo ssingen. Je kunt technische keuzes helder onderbouwen en klanten daarin meenemen, ook als het complex is. Daarin mag je best een tikkeltje eigenwijs zijn.


Nog geen doorgewinterde expert?

Geen probleem. Als je leergierig bent en en affiniteit hebt met data, komen we graag met je in contact.

Persoonlijke vaardigheden:

  • Analytisch sterk, je ziet snel verbanden in data en datastructuren

  • Leergierig en gedreven om jezelf continu te blijven ontwikkelen

  • Zelfstandig maar samenwerkingsgericht, je pakt door zonder dat iemand je hoeft aan te sturen

  • Communicatief vaardig, je vertaalt technische keuzes naar begrijpelijke taal voor klanten

  • Probleemoplossend, je zoekt structurele oplossingen in plaats van tijdelijke fixes

Professionele vaardigheden:

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau in een technische of data-gerelateerde richting

  • 1 tot 3 jaar werkervaring in data engineering of een vergelijkbare consultancy rol

  • Ervaring met ETL/ELT processen, data modeling en data pipelines

Pré:

  • Affiniteit met of kennis van Elastic, SQL of vergelijkbare data-platformen

  • Ervaring met data orchestration, data lakes of dashboarding tools

  • Kennis van cloud omgevingen zoals AWS of Azure

  • Begrijpt hoe data-architectuur bijdraagt aan AI-toepassingen en procesautomatisering


Waarom werken bij PuurData?

Je krijgt de vrijheid om je eigen werkweek in te richten en werkt aan uitdagende projecten bij uiteenlopende klanten, geen saaie repeterende klussen. Je werkt in een platte organisatie waar jouw mening telt en er snel geschakeld wordt. Daarnaast bieden we een salaris passend bij jouw ervaring, pensioen zonder eigen bijdrage en volop ruimte om door te groeien.

Herken jij jezelf hierin? We horen graag van je.

 S.v.p geen acquisitie, wij werven zelf!

Entreprise de référence sur le marché européen des solutions de chauffage, leader sur le marché des énergies nouvelles et renouvelables, véritable centre de compétences industrielles pour la fabrication des ballons d’eau chaude primaire, des ballons thermodynamiques et des équipements solaires.

Apprenti développeur.se fullstack H/F

Le contexte

Notre équipe Industrie 4.0 conçoit et exploite les applications métier de l'usine : collecte de données auprès des machines et des automates, traitement temps réel, écrans d'atelier, suivi et pilotage de la production. Nous développons en interne, sur une stack unifiée, et nos applications tournent en production sur de vraies lignes.

Tes missions

Développement — cœur du poste

  • Développer des fonctionnalités de bout en bout : données, logique serveur, API, interface.
  • Participer aux revues de code, aux tests automatisés et aux pipelines d'intégration continue.
  • Intégrer de nouveaux équipements et de nouvelles sources de données.

Terrain et besoin métier

  • Recueillir le besoin auprès des utilisateurs : opérateurs, régleurs, chefs d'équipe, méthodes, qualité, maintenance.
  • Rédiger les cahiers des charges et les spécifications fonctionnelles.
  • Démontrer, former, recueillir les retours, itérer.

Déploiement

  • Participer aux mises en service au pied des machines : raccordement, configuration, validation sur site, documentation.
  • Contribuer au diagnostic des incidents en production.

Gestion de projet

  • Porter un sujet de bout en bout : cadrage, découpage, suivi, livraison.

Notre stack

TypeScript de bout en bout

  • Nuxt / Vue 3
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Node
  • PostgreSQL
  • WebSocket
  • Docker
  • GitLab CI/CD
  • Linux
  • protocoles industriels (OPC-UA, Siemens S7)

Le profil

Attendu

  • Bases solides en JavaScript / TypeScript, dont l'asynchrone.
  • Un framework web à composants déjà pratiqué (idéalement Vue, sinon React ou Angular).
  • Bases de données relationnelles et SQL.
  • Git, ligne de commande Linux, notions de réseau IP.

Apprécié

  • Une première expérience en milieu industriel (stage, alternance, job d'été en production, maintenance ou bureau d'études) : c'est un vrai plus, comprendre une ligne de production ne s'improvise pas.
  • Notions d'automatismes, Docker, CI/CD, tests automatisés.
  • Anglais technique.

Ce qui compte autant que la technique

  • Aller sur le terrain volontiers : une partie du travail se fait en atelier, debout, en chaussures de sécurité.
  • Savoir parler à des non-informaticiens et traduire dans les deux sens.
  • Savoir écrire : une spec et une doc sont des livrables.
  • Rigueur : ce qui est déployé pilote de la production réelle.

À savoir

  • Poste en présentiel sur site.
  • EPI fournis.

Ce que tu en retires

Une expérience full-stack réelle sur des applications en production, la pratique complète du cycle besoin → spec → développement → tests → déploiement → exploitation, et une compétence recherchée : le pont entre l'informatique et le monde industriel. Accompagnement par un développeur référent, montée en autonomie progressive.

Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization.We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.

  • We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.
  • We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey.
  • We're designing the future of autonomous marketing, taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do.

And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine — Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

We want you to join us full-time as a Staff Backend Engineer. You will work remotely first (from Central & Eastern Europe), but we are more than happy to meet you in our nice offices in Bratislava, Brno or Prague.

The Pulsar team builds platform and admin services that all Bloomreach SaaS products rely on. In your first year, you’ll develop features used by thousands of customers and deliver fast, consistent, and high-energy (but low-drama) product releases. We all work remotely from the US, India, and Europe.

Examples of our services:

  • Central services to publish Model Context Protocol APIs for external AI agents
  • Multi-product customer provisioning and licensing orchestration
  • Integrated user management, authentication, and authorization
  • High-availability, centralized configuration management
  • Tools for new customer integration & product tuning

Why you’ll love your work

  • Technical Variety: Cloud-native services with diverse tech stacks offer learning and experimentation.
  • Impact: Our services are used by customers and teams across the company – engineers, product managers, services consultants, and even executives.
  • Autonomy: Senior engineers design, build, and deploy complete projects and are experts in our services.
  • Teamwork: Your teammates are also high performers and will support you with learning our systems, brainstorming & design review, and running high-reliability production deployments.

Your typical day

Your day begins with review of a teammate’s GitLab merge request. It has already been reviewed by Claude, but you’ll think deeply about the business problem, alternative solutions, and future needs.

Then you spend a few undisturbed hours “in the flow,” working on a technical design doc for a new project. Once you’ve completed a draft, you send it to another teammate for feedback, then decide to jump on a Zoom call to talk it over and refine it.

After lunch, you join the team for a quick standup via Zoom to discuss current work and the plan for the next few days. You mention that you’re finishing up a small improvement to improve the logging and alerting for one of our components that requires high uptime. A teammate offers to review your changes. It has some complex behavior, so you walk through it together and make a few improvements.

Soon, the new unit tests are green. With a few keystrokes, you create a merge request, spin up a dev instance, and deploy your change. After some quick smoke tests, you and your teammate decide to merge the change. Your improvement will be deployed in production with the release in a few days.

Next, you respond to a Slack request for advice on integrating with the authorization API. You draft a short tech design doc that links the API spec, code examples, and optimization tips. You discuss it on the team channel, and your manager forwards it to another team that’s also starting a new service.

Your day ends with a chat with a product manager about questions that came up while drafting the tech design. With their feedback, you refine the proposal to deliver the core feature more quickly, while the product manager will work with customers and decide how much more to invest. Tomorrow, you’ll break down the tasks in Jira and decide what you’ll complete yourself and what you’ll ask teammates to complete….

Our tech stack(s)

  • Languages & Frameworks: Java / Spring, Python, Go – occasionally TypeScript, Angular, React
  • Data: Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka
  • Cloud: AWS & GCP (RDS, Redshift, Pub/Sub, BigTable, DataFlow, etc), Docker & Kubernetes (via EKS & GKE)
  • Tools: Jira, Gitlab CI/CD, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch

Our expectations

  • Flexible intelligence: Stretch your technical skills in a distributed cloud environment, making changes across systems built with various tech stacks to meet challenging requirements.
  • Drive: Rapidly ship product improvements that affect thousands of users in a low-drama and high-trust way.
  • Security & Reliability: Balance risks and benefits of change with discipline and agility.
  • Communication: Organize technical work and maintain trust/respect across multiple teams, geographic regions, and departments.
  • Knowledge Sharing: Proactively share expertise, guide less experienced team members, and document work for long-term sustainability.

The ideal candidate’s experience

  • Active user of AI coding tools such as Cursor and Claude Code
  • Developed backend services with Python using a variety of data systems (5+ years)
  • Understands web security principles (OWASP), Authentication, and Authorization practices
  • Designed APIs for a SaaS product
  • Operated services in production on public cloud infrastructure
  • Some experience with Java / Spring or Go
  • Exposure to web frontend development (Angular / React)

Our reps spend most of their day in Salesforce, and how it feels to use directly affects how much they sell. We're hiring a Salesforce Developer with a UI/UX focus to redesign the rep experience across our Sales and Revenue teams. You'll join the global Salesforce team for 12 months to make the CRM faster, clearer and more intuitive.

This is a hands-on build role. You'll design the experience and code it in Lightning Web Components, working with Sales, RevOps, Marketing and Data, and directly with the reps who use the result.


What You Will Do


Redesign the rep experience

  • Audit the current Lightning experience (record pages, console apps, list views, home pages) and find where reps lose time to clicks, clutter and missing context.

  • Turn what you find into a prioritised roadmap of UI improvements tied to rep productivity and adoption.

  • Design and prototype improved layouts, workflows and components, and validate them with reps before building.

Build with LWC

  • Develop custom Lightning Web Components (and supporting Apex where needed) that replace clunky standard layouts with focused, usable interfaces.

  • Configure and extend Lightning App Builder pages, Dynamic Forms, Dynamic Actions and console apps to deliver a consistent experience across teams and regions.

  • Build reusable components and follow SLDS conventions so the UI stays consistent and maintainable after your contract ends.

Make it stick

  • Run feedback sessions, usability tests and pilots with reps and managers, and iterate on the results.

  • Track adoption, page performance and user satisfaction to show what each release changed.

  • Create release notes, short walkthroughs and handover documentation so changes land well and the team can maintain what you build.

Work as part of the global team

  • Work within the global team's standards for source control, code review, sandboxes and release management.

  • Partner with admins, architects and data teams so UI changes fit the wider data model, security model and automation.

  • Pass on what you learn about Lightning UX patterns and LWC best practices to the wider team.


What You Will Need


Must have

  • Strong, demonstrable experience building Lightning Web Components in production.

  • Solid Apex, SOQL and Salesforce data model knowledge to support your components.

  • Deep knowledge of Lightning Experience customisation: App Builder, Dynamic Forms, page layouts, console apps and Flows.

  • Experience with Salesforce DX, Git and a CI/CD or deployment process.

  • A UX mindset: you start from user problems, can explain design decisions, and can take feedback from non-technical users.

  • Clear communication and the ability to work independently across time zones in a global team.

Nice to have

  • Portfolio or examples of Salesforce UI work you've shipped (screenshots or demos are ideal).

  • Experience with SLDS, Figma or similar prototyping tools, and accessibility (WCAG) principles.

  • Experience in Sales Cloud, especially rep-facing workflows such as opportunity management, account planning and pipeline views.

  • Jest testing for LWC, and Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer I/II, JavaScript Developer I, Platform App Builder).

  • Experience with performance profiling and optimisation in Lightning pages.


What Success Looks Like (12 Months)

  • Month 3: UX audit complete and a prioritised roadmap agreed with Sales leadership.

  • Month 6: First wave of redesigned pages and components live for a pilot group, with adoption and feedback baselined.

  • Month 12: Redesigned experience rolled out to target teams, a maintained component library in place, and full documentation handed to the global team.

  • Flexible compensation options to help your money go further.

  • 17 weeks of paid parental leave during your child’s first year.

  • 16 paid volunteer hours each year to give back to causes you care about.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. ecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.


Why This Role Matters

You build and run the platform the whole product sits on: the event streams, the backend services and the cloud infrastructure everything else is built on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to make sure that traffic lands reliably, moves through the system in a shape other teams can build on, and keeps doing so as the number of sites grows.
You join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.

What you will work on

  • Event streaming. Kafka is the spine of the system. You own topic and schema design, partitioning, retention and delivery semantics  and the everyday reality behind them: consumers falling behind, replays, backfills, late and duplicated readings.
  • Backend services in TypeScript. The ingestion services, integrations and APIs around that stream. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is turning that variety into one consistent interface the product squads can rely on.
  • Cloud infrastructure on GCP. Compute, networking, IAM, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. The goal is a paved road: other engineers ship and debug their own services without going through you.
  • Technical direction. You are senior enough to set it. Where we invest in the platform, what we standardise, what we deliberately leave rough for now  and bringing the rest of the team along with it.


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • At least 6–8 years building and running backend systems in production, including real time in a platform or infrastructure role that other engineers depended on
  • Strong backend engineering in TypeScript. You have designed, shipped and operated services and APIs in it — not just touched it around the edges of a frontend
  • Hands-on with Kafka in production. Topic design, consumer groups, ordering and delivery guarantees, and what you actually do at 3am when a consumer group is hours behind. A comparable streaming platform is fine if you know it at that depth
  • Solid on GCP or an equivalent cloud: containers, networking and IAM basics, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting. You have owned infrastructure, not just deployed onto it

Why Integrations Engineering at Langfuse

Your work puts Langfuse into developers’ hands.

Our SDKs are downloaded 26M+ times per month, and for many developers the first thing they touch is an integration — a few lines of code that connect their favorite framework to Langfuse. When that experience is seamless, they’re wow’ed. When it’s not, we might have lost them. You’ll own that critical first impression across 40+ framework integrations.

You’ll live at the frontier of LLM application development.

The AI framework ecosystem moves fast — new agent frameworks, orchestration libraries, and model providers emerge every week. You’ll be among the first to instrument them, giving you unmatched exposure to how cutting-edge AI applications are built. The developers you serve are some of the most ambitious software engineers in the world, and working closely with them will make you an expert on LLM engineering yourself.

Everything you build is open source and immediately visible.

All Langfuse integrations are MIT-licensed. When you ship a new integration or improve an existing one, thousands of developers benefit the same day — and they’ll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on Twitter, and in our community channels.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Build and maintain framework integrations. Langfuse integrates with 40+ frameworks and model providers: OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, and many more. You’ll own these integrations end-to-end — from initial implementation to ongoing maintenance as frameworks evolve. When a new framework gains traction, you’ll be among the first to instrument it.

  • Design new integration patterns for emerging frameworks. When a framework or a new agent orchestrator appears, you’ll evaluate it, design the right instrumentation approach (callback handler, decorator, OTEL auto-instrumentation, or a combination), build the integration, write the docs, and ship it. You’ll develop strong opinions on what makes a great integration experience.

  • Contribute to the core SDKs. While integrations are your primary focus, your work will surface needs in our Python and TypeScript SDKs. You’ll contribute improvements to the core SDK when your integration work demands it — whether that’s a new hook point, better context propagation, or performance optimizations.

  • Write documentation and integration guides. At Langfuse, docs are part of our core product. When you ship a new integration, the guide ships with it. You’ll own the integration docs, quickstart tutorials, cookbooks, and migration paths that help developers get started in minutes.

  • Be a voice in the developer community. You’ll engage with framework communities, respond to integration-related GitHub issues, write blog posts about new integrations, and be present in our Slack/Discord channels. You’ll build relationships with framework maintainers and represent Langfuse in the broader AI developer ecosystem.

What We’re Looking For

  • Passionate about the LLM ecosystem. You’ve built real applications with frameworks like LangChain, Pydantic AI, Vercel AI SDK, LlamaIndex, or similar — or you have a deep willingness to go deep and get your hands dirty with every major framework in the space. You’re excited about this ecosystem, not just familiar with it.

  • Strong in Python and/or TypeScript. You write clean, reliable code. You don’t need to be a systems-level performance expert, but you care about code quality and understand that integrations run inside other people’s production systems.

  • Product-minded engineer. You think about the developer who’s going to use your integration at 11pm trying to ship a feature. You obsess over the getting-started experience: how many lines of code does it take? Is the error message helpful? Does the docs example actually work?

  • Self-directed and motivated. You know how to develop conviction about what to build and how to ship it. You don’t wait for detailed specs — you investigate the framework, talk to users, and propose the right approach.

  • Excited about open source and developer community. You genuinely enjoy talking to developers about their integration challenges, writing clear documentation, and contributing to open source projects.

  • Thrives in a small, accountable team. Your output is visible and matters. You’re comfortable owning outcomes, not just tasks.

CS or quantitative degree preferred, but not required. We care far more about what you’ve built and your hunger to learn.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with OpenTelemetry internals or observability instrumentation

  • Contributions to popular open source projects, SDKs, or developer tools

  • Experience building developer tooling, CLIs, or client libraries

  • Former founder or early startup experience

  • Active presence in AI/ML developer communities (blog posts, talks, open source)

 

No candidate checks all boxes. If you feel you are a good fit for this role, please go ahead and apply.

 

Projects You Could Own

  • Build and ship a Langfuse integration for an emerging agent framework (e.g., OpenClaw, new OTEL-based instrumentation)

  • Design the integration pattern for a new category of AI tools (e.g., voice agents via LiveKit/Pipecat)

  • Create comprehensive quickstart cookbooks that get developers from zero to traced in under 5 minutes

  • Work with the OpenTelemetry community to improve GenAI semantic conventions

  • Maintain and upgrade our most popular integrations (OpenAI, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK) as those frameworks ship breaking changes

 

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

• We are hiring a Senior Platform Engineer (m/f/d) to become the second senior voice in Platform, alongside our DevOps Lead, and to bridge two worlds he cannot cover alone: application-level developer experience and data engineering
  • You will build the automation foundation for the manual data quality checks a single team member has held for years and is now transitioning out of.
  • You keep our analytics layer running while planning its successor. You raise developer experience as a measurable discipline. You are hands-on, you write code daily, and you set the standard for how the engineering group builds and ships
  • Own Application & DevEx in the Platform group. Developer frameworks, application-level tooling, framework upgrades (NestJS, TypeScript ecosystem), test infrastructure, local dev flow, build pipelines. You define “how we build at Cozero” and reduce friction across the engineering group
  • Lead the data platform infrastructure. Warehouse and operational database architecture, cost and performance tuning (Snowflake and Postgres, or similar), orchestration (Dagster, Airflow, or equivalent), ingestion and CDC pipelines, transformation layer, environments and deployment for data workloads, and the infrastructure for AI and ML workloads: serving and inference, LLM application infra, evaluation and versioning, cost control. You work closely with our DevOps lead on the layers underneath. You provide the paved path; Data and Engineering build on top of it
  • Make data reliability an engineering discipline. Pipeline observability, lineage, data quality checks, alerting and freshness SLOs, test coverage for transformations. Convert tribal knowledge and manual checks into maintained, observable, test-covered systems
  • Raise developer experience as a discipline. Build times, test flakiness, local dev flow, repo hygiene, framework upgrade cadence. You measure these and reduce them. AI-assisted tooling (Claude Code, Cursor) is part of the toolkit, and you push the team’s fluency here. Eg building skills, agents or Bots to expedite our delivery speed with solid quality gates
  • Participate in the on-call rotation. Every senior engineer, including platform, takes a turn as primary or backup on a 2-week cycle
  • Mentor across squads. Your work touches every squad’s daily experience. Fast, actionable code and design reviews

Benefits

  • 27 days of vacation: We offer 27 days of paid time off on top of national holidays, no matter where you are based
  • VSOP: As a valued team member, you’ll have the opportunity to join our VSOP pool, allowing you to share in the company’s financial success
  • Flexible working hours: Trust is the backbone of our culture, so you have the autonomy to set your own work hours. We recognize that work-life balance varies for each individual, so you are encouraged to adjust your schedule to suit your personal needs, whether that’s spending time with family or focusing on your health and well-being
  • Learning budget: You will have a budget of EUR 500 per year to allocate towards any learning and development activities of your choice. You have the freedom to select whatever you believe is best for your growth
  • Work from home budget: You will receive a one-off payment of EUR 500 to purchase any equipment you need for your remote office. We provide you with a Mac
  • Work from anywhere: We fully embrace remote work and its flexibility. However, we must adhere to the tax regulations specific to each country
  • In-person Gatherings: There’s nothing like in-person connections to boost team spirit. That’s why we organize two types of gatherings: company-wide events twice a year and team-focused meetups twice a year
  • Have taken over a system from a single point of failure. You know how to do knowledge transfer well: pair sessions, written runbooks, shadowing, gradual ownership handover
  • Are AI-native in your engineering practice. Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, integrated into your daily flow. You use AI to move faster on framework work, refactoring, and repetitive automation. You have opinions on where AI helps and where it does not
  • Have 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years in a senior IC role owning developer platform, developer experience, or data platform work
  • Have shipped data quality automation. Great Expectations, dbt tests, custom frameworks, or your own thing. Duplicate detection, outlier flagging, schema drift, and lineage are all patterns you have implemented
  • Communicate in writing first. RFCs, tech docs, decision records. Async by default, but you’re not afraid to “pick up the phone” to rapidly unblock yourself, instead of waiting for a fixed meeting
  • Have straddled backend and data engineering deliberately. You are fluent in TypeScript / NestJS and comfortable in Python. You have built ETL pipelines, worked with a warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or equivalent), and shipped systems where data correctness matters
  • Have owned developer experience as a first-class product. Build pipelines, test infrastructure, framework upgrades, local dev flow. You have measured DevEx metrics (build time, PR turnaround, flake rate) and moved them
  • Have opinions about test infrastructure at scale. Unit vs integration vs E2E, contract testing, data test fixtures, test parallelisation. You have made these choices in a real codebase and can defend them
  • Are comfortable with ambiguity. The Application & DevEx charter is broad. You will shape it as much as inherit it
  • Go deep on the warehouse and the operational database rather than treating either as a black box. You can reason about Snowflake or similar structures, dynamic tables, warehouse sizing, and query cost, and you have shipped data quality automation: duplicate detection, outlier flagging, schema drift, lineage, whether with dbt tests, a dedicated validation framework, or your own
  • Experience in climate tech, carbon accounting, or sustainability platforms
  • Experience with Prisma ORM at scale
  • Experience replacing a legacy analytics layer (CubeJS, Looker, Metabase, or equivalent) with a modern stack
  • Experience automating manual data checks into production systems
  • Nx or similar monorepo tooling experience

About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s newest unicorns with a team of just over 700 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot )

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership across a broad remit. You are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people, who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  3. Build the best technology in-house , using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior PHP Engineer based in Mexico to help grow Lenda, our credit card product for the Mexican market.

You’ll join a small, cross-functional team with a startup mindset, backed by one of Europe’s most successful and profitable fintechs. You’ll play a key role in scaling a new product, with significant ownership and the opportunity to shape how we build from an early stage.

We’re looking for an experienced, resourceful engineer who can collaborate across Product, Backend and Frontend, leverage learnings from our established products, shape API and technical decisions, and work closely with stakeholders to deliver customer value quickly.

Our tech stack

We believe in using the right tools for the job, and our stack reflects our commitment to modern, efficient development:

  • Backend: PHP 8, Symfony, AWS, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes

  • CI/CD: Datadog, GitHub Actions and ArgoCD

  • Testing & Monitoring: Behat, PHPUnit for robust automated testing, Datadog for monitoring

  • Productivity: Github, Slack, Jira & Confluence

What we're looking for

We're seeking passionate engineers who are excited to contribute and grow with us

Must have:

  • Based either Mexico or willing to relocate to Mexico

  • Must have strong English language skills (written and spoken)

  • High degree of ownership and autonomy

  • Strong, business oriented, engineer with modern PHP development experience (PHP 8.0+ is a must). You're fluent in the latest PHP features and best practices.

  • A solid grasp of a modern PHP framework like Symfony or Laravel .

  • Experience with Domain Driven Design, Message-Driven Systems, Event Sourcing and CQRS

  • Excellent automated testing skills (unit, integration, functional) - you believe in quality code.

  • A genuine desire to learn, collaborate, and contribute your ideas within a highly collaborative team .

Nice to have:

  • Familiarity with microservices architecture and working on financial systems is a bonus.

  • You have experimented with AI tooling to accelerate your own, and others, productivity, and can discuss the positives and negatives of different approaches and tools

  • Experience in a cross-functional environment .

Interview process

  • Short video call with one of our team members to learn more about each other, and answer any initial questions you have about the role

  • Cognitive Assessment

  • Technical session with your peers where you’ll discuss your solution to the exercise, talk through some problems and scenarios, and dig deeper into your technical experience
